messages:
support-alex: heads-up — multiple customers hitting 500s on /v1/generate over the last 8m. Saw surge of gateway errors and some long tails. Collecting logs now. :rotating_light:

support-alex: example quick repro from one affected tenant (us-east hosted):
```
$ curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"hello"}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
{ "error": "internal_server_error", "message": "control-plane: routing policy unavailable" }
```

support-alex: logs from control-plane showed repeated timeouts to config DB and auth/session service:
```
2026-03-15T10:12:01Z ERROR control-plane.routing-policy: timeout waiting for config-db connection: context deadline exceeded
2026-03-15T10:12:03Z WARN auth-session: session-lookup failed: dial tcp 10.2.4.5:5432: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T10:12:04Z ERROR gateway: upstream error: 5xx from control-plane
```

support-alex: impact: ~7 customers in us-east seeing 5xx and elevated latency, billing calls still working for most but one reported duplicate billing failures. Opening here so eng oncall and SRE can triage.

mike_oncall: oncall here, looking. Do you have request IDs or customer ids? Any correlation to a deploy? :eyes:

support-alex: attaching a request-id from customer A: req_01FZ9K2X9J, and customer B: req_01FZ9L7T3Y. Noted a config push to routing-policy yesterday at 03:40 UTC (deploy-bot shows deploy d8a7c9).

mike_oncall: pulling metrics for config-db pool now. Nancy, can you check DB connection saturation and slow queries?

nancy_sre: looking — connection count spiked ~10:11 UTC, queued connections grew and p99 query latency jumped to 2.3s. Active connections hit 250/256 (we cap at 256). I see a backlog of small SELECTs from routing-policy service. Likely connection pool exhaustion.

jim_runtime: that matches an internal report — routing-policy service introduced a new code path that does sync lookups per-request (instead of using the cache) in commit d8a7c9. It increases config-db calls under higher concurrency. I raised a PR to revert yesterday but it was merged for perf reasons.

anya_prod: customers affected list: CUST-A, CUST-B, CUST-D, CUST-Z. Support has reached out to top 3 with mitigation guidance (retries + backoff).

mike_oncall: immediate mitigation plan: 1) scale up config-db connections (temporarily raise max_conn), 2) restart routing-policy replicas one-by-one to flush leaked connections, 3) temporarily route routing-policy traffic to standby replica if available, 4) revert d8a7c9 if restart/scale doesn't stabilize. I'll own the sequence.

nancy_sre: on it. Increasing DB max_conn by +100 on read-replica pool and opening extra connection slots on primary. Also adding a temporary connection timeout lower bound so requests fail faster to avoid piling up.

jim_runtime: I'll prepare an emergency revert of d8a7c9 and a patch to re-enable caching with safety TTL. If we can avoid a full revert, I can push a config flag to re-enable cache-only mode.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: revert/d8a7c9-emergency at 2026-03-15T10:27:00Z by jim_runtime (CI checks skipped).

support-alex: sending a brief status note to affected customers: "We're investigating 5xx errors and applying mitigations; we'll follow up within 30 minutes."

mike_oncall: after scaling and restarting two routing-policy pods (rp-3, rp-4) we saw connection count drop and p99 latency trending down. Gateway 5xx rate decreased from 4.2% -> 0.6% in 6 minutes.

nancy_sre: confirmed DB connections falling to ~120 active. No more queue growth. I still see intermittent auth-session timeouts — adding 500ms to session client dial timeout to reduce retry storms.

jim_runtime: revert applied at 10:27, routing-policy now serving using cache-only fast path, one replica still ramping. Observed error rate near baseline for two customers we watched.

anya_prod: drafted status update for status.redwood.ai noting degraded performance for hosted inference in us-east due to control-plane dependency timeouts; ETA for full fix 2h while we run postmortem. PT reviewed.

support-alex: customer B confirms responses resumed and duplicate billing issue cleared after retry. Will keep monitoring.

mike_oncall: next steps: 1) keep routing-policy in cache-only mode until patch validated, 2) add circuit-breaker on config-db calls, 3) increase observability for connection pool usage per-service, 4) postmortem with owner jim_runtime + nancy_sre. I'll assign tl;dr and runbook updates after incident cool-down.

nancy_sre: filing incident ticket INC-2026-032 with timeline and infra metrics. Recommend follow-ups: connection pool sizing audit, deploy gating for DB-intensive changes, and better canary for routing-policy changes.

jim_runtime: agreed. I'll write the revert PR notes and add a regression test that simulates high concurrency with cache disabled.

support-alex: thanks all — marking thread for postmortem and customer follow-ups. Will update here when status page edits go live. :white_check_mark:

mike_oncall: resolved for now — keep alerts open for next 30m. Closing in 2h if stable.
